# Business Cards

> An offline contact-card sharer. You keep several cards (contact details plus
> social handles) on your own phone; tapping a row fills the screen with a QR
> code the person opposite scans with their camera. The important one carries a
> vCard *inside the code*, so it works with no network on either phone and needs
> no app installed on theirs. No backend, no accounts, no analytics.

Live: https://venkatamutyala.github.io/business-cards/
Source: https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards
Licence: MIT. Vendored third-party code is listed in NOTICE.md.

Vanilla ES modules. **No build step, no dependencies, no package.json.** Edit a
file and reload. Everything runs in Docker; nothing is installed on the host.

## How it is put together

- [index.html](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/index.html): one page; each screen is a section, toggled by `hidden`
- [js/ui.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/ui.js): home list, card switcher, backup & transfer sheet, and the `showSurface()` state machine
- [js/qrview.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/qrview.js): the full-screen QR overlay — an overlay, deliberately not one of the surfaces
- [js/store.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/store.js): localStorage, validation, the forward-only migration chain, backup signature
- [js/codec.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/codec.js): the `#p=` payload — deflate-raw, base64url, one marker byte
- [js/rows.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/rows.js): the service registry; adding a service is ONE entry here
- [js/vcard.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/vcard.js): vCard 3.0 builder, escaping, length budget with a drop order
- [js/qr.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/js/qr.js): canvas rendering and the integer-scaling maths
- [tests/cases.js](https://github.com/venkatamutyala/business-cards/blob/main/tests/cases.js): one assertion table, run by `node:test` and by `/tests/test.html` in a browser

## Running and testing

```sh
docker compose up -d                              # nginx :8080 + an HTTPS tunnel
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app node:22-alpine \
  node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/unit.test.js
```

The browser runner at `/tests/test.html` matters more than the Node one: opened
on a phone it executes where the platform differences actually are.

## Decisions that look like bugs and are not

If you are changing this code, these are deliberate. Each was arrived at the
hard way; please do not "fix" one without reading why.

- **Error correction is hardcoded L, and L is a floor, not a default.** A screen
  has no damage to correct for. The real failure is moiré from the camera
  sampling the display grid, and bigger modules prevent that — which beats
  correcting for it. Raising ECC makes codes *harder* to scan here.
- **The quiet zone is drawn into the canvas**, not left to CSS, so it survives a
  screenshot or "save image".
- **No swipe navigation on the QR screen.** For the seconds that matter the
  phone faces away from its owner, who cannot see it. An accidental swipe would
  silently swap the code and they would scan the wrong thing. Same reason for
  the grip margins, the edge-swipe rejection and the recipient-facing caption.
- **`active` is excluded from the backup signature** in `canonical()`. Including
  it would mean merely *switching cards* reported your backup as stale, and a
  chip that lies is one people stop reading.
- **The v1 payload fixture in `tests/cases.js` must never be regenerated.**
  Encoding and decoding with current code passes whether or not migration works;
  only a real historical payload proves the chain still holds.
- **`facetime:` is intentionally outside `ALLOWED_SCHEMES` but inside
  `RENDERABLE_SCHEMES`.** The first list gates data arriving from a payload; the
  second gates URLs the app builds from its own registry.
- **Every path is relative** (`./`), including `start_url`, `scope` and the
  service-worker registration, so the app runs from any subpath. Introducing an
  absolute path breaks every fork.
- **Payload data reaches the DOM through `textContent` only.** There is no
  `innerHTML` anywhere and it should stay that way.
- **`sw.js` serves cache-first and never calls `skipWaiting()` on its own.** An
  update waits for the user to tap Reload; the app must not reload itself out
  from under someone mid-handover.

## Fork it

Fork, then Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → `main` / `/ (root)`.
Nothing needs editing. One caveat: `localStorage` is per-origin, not per-path,
so on `<you>.github.io/<repo>/` the cards share a bucket with that account's
other Pages projects.
